0|Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and Medicare Part D Contract Network|"# Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and Medicare Part D Contract Network

The community centers on the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) as the central governing authority overseeing Medicare Part D, a federal prescription drug benefit program. Key entities include CMS, Prescription Drug Plan (PDP) Sponsors, regulatory frameworks such as 42 CFR §§ 423.521 and 423.522, and critical guidance documents like the 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions and the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual. These entities are interconnected through formal contractual relationships, regulatory compliance obligations, and operational guidance, with CMS serving as the primary enforcer and coordinator of program standards. The network reflects a tightly structured federal oversight system designed to ensure beneficiary access, cost containment, and regulatory adherence across private plan sponsors.

## Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services as the central governing authority

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is the central entity in this community, acting as the federal agency responsible for administering Medicare Part D and overseeing all contractual relationships with Prescription Drug Plan (PDP) Sponsors. CMS establishes the rules, standards, and guidelines that govern the program, including formulary requirements, pricing, network adequacy, and quality of care. It manages the entire lifecycle of Medicare Part D contracts, from solicitation of applications to final settlement and appeals. CMS also monitors sponsor performance to ensure compliance with federal regulations and to protect beneficiaries’ interests. Its role extends beyond oversight to include policy development, payment rate setting, and program reform implementation. As a key component of the Department of Health and Human Services, CMS ensures transparency and accountability in the delivery of prescription drug benefits to older adults and individuals with disabilities. [Data: Entities (0), Relationships (0, 274, 275, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 279, 280, +more)]

## Regulatory and procedural framework governing PDP sponsor compliance

The community is governed by a robust set of regulations and procedural documents that define how PDP Sponsors must operate. Key among these is 42 CFR §§ 423.521 and 423.522, which outline the final settlement process, payment mechanisms, and appeals procedures for Medicare Part D plans. These regulations are binding on PDP Sponsors and ensure consistency and fairness in financial and administrative processes. The PDP Sponsor is subject to these rules through formal contractual relationships, and non-compliance can result in penalties or contract termination. The regulations are reinforced by other foundational documents such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual and the 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, which provide detailed operational guidance. Together, these documents create a comprehensive compliance framework that ensures all sponsors adhere to federal standards. [Data: Entities (152, 6, 8), Relationships (274, 49, 57, +more)]

## Critical guidance documents shaping program operations and beneficiary access

CMS issues a suite of final guidance documents that directly influence how PDP Sponsors administer the Medicare Part D program. The Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions outline changes to benefit structures and plan operations, requiring sponsors to adapt their offerings to meet new federal mandates. Similarly, the Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance details how pharmaceutical manufacturers must provide discounts to reduce beneficiary costs, impacting plan formularies and pricing models. The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance enables beneficiaries to pay for drugs in installments, increasing affordability and access. These documents are not advisory but are incorporated into contracts and must be implemented by sponsors. They are disseminated through official channels such as CMS Participant Guides and Health Plan Management System memos, ensuring widespread awareness and compliance. [Data: Entities (8, 9, 10, 11, 12), Relationships (5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 57, +more)]

## Formal contract lifecycle managed through structured solicitation and documentation

The community operates through a formal contract lifecycle initiated by the 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, issued on January 9, 2024. This solicitation serves as a binding document that invites entities to apply for the 2025 contract year, setting the stage for the formation of new agreements between CMS and PDP Sponsors. The solicitation incorporates the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual as a foundational component of the contract, ensuring that all sponsors operate under a unified set of rules. The contract itself is formalized through the application of a date stamp and the assignment of a contract name, both of which are critical for legal and administrative validity. The contract is signed by Vanessa S. Duran, Director of the Medicare Drug Benefit and C & D Data Group at CMS, affirming the agency’s official commitment. This structured process ensures transparency, accountability, and enforceability across all contractual relationships. [Data: Entities (4, 150, 154, 155), Relationships (279, 280, 49, 275, +more)]

## Integration of manufacturer discount programs into plan operations

The Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program is a critical component of the community’s cost-containment strategy. This federal program requires pharmaceutical manufacturers to provide discounts on certain drugs to Medicare Part D plans, directly reducing beneficiary costs. The program is governed by 42 CFR § 423.286, which affects premium calculations and cost-sharing mechanisms. PDP Sponsors must incorporate these discounts into their formularies and pricing models, ensuring that beneficiaries receive the full benefit of reduced drug prices. The program’s implementation is guided by CMS’s final guidance and is integrated into the broader operational framework through the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual. This integration ensures that sponsors comply with federal mandates and that beneficiaries receive equitable access to affordable medications. The program exemplifies how federal policy is operationalized through regulatory and contractual mechanisms. [Data: Entities (27, 152, 112), Relationships (112, 6, 57, +more)]

## Role of CMS in disseminating operational guidance and ensuring compliance

CMS plays a proactive role in ensuring that PDP Sponsors understand and comply with program requirements through multiple communication channels. These include CMS Participant Guides, which provide detailed instructions on compliance with Part D rules; Health Plan Management System memos, which deliver real-time operational updates and policy clarifications; and formal training sessions conducted by CMS. These tools are essential for maintaining consistency across sponsors, especially as program rules evolve. The rate announcement, another key document, provides annual updates on premium rates and benefit levels, which are used to inform contract terms and sponsor bidding. Together, these mechanisms create a continuous feedback loop between CMS and sponsors, enabling timely adaptation to regulatory changes. The effectiveness of this guidance system is critical to the program’s success, as it reduces the risk of non-compliance and ensures equitable service delivery. [Data: Entities (11, 12, 13, 14), Relationships (8, 9, 10, 11, 57, +more)]

## High degree of interdependence among regulatory, operational, and administrative entities

The community demonstrates a high degree of interdependence among its key entities, where each component relies on others to function effectively. For example, the 2025 Solicitation for Applications incorporates the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, which in turn integrates the Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions. This cascading relationship ensures that all sponsors receive a unified set of rules. Similarly, the Manufacturer Discount Program affects premium calculations, which are then reflected in the rate announcement and incorporated into contract terms. The date stamp and contract name are not standalone identifiers but are part of a larger legal and administrative framework that validates the contract’s execution. The signing of the contract by Vanessa S. Duran formalizes the agency’s authority and commitment. This interconnectedness underscores the complexity and precision required in managing the Medicare Part D program, where changes in one area can have ripple effects across the entire network. [Data: Entities (4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 13, 154, 155, 150), Relationships (49, 57, 112, 274, 275, 279, 280, +more)]"

1. If a PDP Sponsor uses a standard for reimbursement of pharmacies based on the cost of a drug, PDP Sponsor will update such standard not less frequently than once every 7 days, beginning with an initial update on January 1 of each year, to accurately reflect the market price of the drug.

Sponsor will disclose all individual drug prices to be updated to the applicable pharmacies in advance for their use for the reimbursement of claims.

## A. RECORD MAINTENANCE AND ACCESS

PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain records and provide access in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(10) and 423.505(i)(2).

## B. GENERAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit information to CMS according to 42 CFR §§ 423.505(f) and 423.514, and applicable Final Medicare Part D Reporting Guidance.

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit to CMS each plan's formulary information, including any changes to its formularies, and hereby grants to the Government, and any person or entity who might receive the formulary from the Government, a non-exclusive license to use all or any portion of the formulary for any purpose related to the administration of the Part D program, including without limitation publicly distributing, displaying, publishing, or reconfiguration of the information in any medium, including www.medicare.gov, and by any electronic, print, or other means of distribution.

## Article IV HIPAA Provisions

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the confidentiality and enrollee record accuracy requirements specified in 42 CFR § 423.136.
- B. PDP Sponsor agrees to enter into a business associate agreement with the entity with which CMS has contracted to track Medicare beneficiaries' true out-of- pocket costs.

Article V

## Requirements of Other Laws and Regulations

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with (a) applicable Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including, but not limited to, applicable provisions of Federal criminal law, the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729 et seq.), and the anti-kickback provision of § 1128B of the Act; (b) applicable Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) rules at 45 CFR Parts 160, 162, and 164; and (c) all other applicable Federal statutes and regulations.

This contract is effective from the date of CMS's authorized representative's signature through December 31, 2025. This contract shall be renewable for successive one-year periods thereafter according to 42 CFR § 423.506.

1. In accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507, PDP Sponsor will be determined qualified to renew its contract annually only if PDP Sponsor has not provided CMS with a notice of intention not to renew in accordance with Article VII of this contract.

114|FIRST MONDAY OF JUNE|The FIRST MONDAY OF JUNE serves as a critical deadline for Part D Prescription Drug Plan (PDP) Sponsors in the United States. On this date, PDP Sponsors are required to notify the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) of their intent not to renew a Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug (MA-PD) contract for the upcoming plan year. This deadline ensures that CMS has sufficient time to process nonrenewal notifications and manage the transition of beneficiaries to new or alternative coverage options. The requirement applies to all PDP Sponsors who wish to discontinue their participation in the Medicare Part D program for the following year, and timely submission of nonrenewal intent is essential to maintain compliance with federal regulations. Failure to meet this deadline may result in unintended continuation of the contract, potentially leading to administrative and financial consequences for the sponsor. The FIRST MONDAY OF JUNE is therefore a fixed, annual date that provides a standardized timeline for plan sponsors to make strategic decisions about their participation in the Medicare program. It reflects the broader regulatory framework designed to ensure continuity of care and stability in the Medicare Part D marketplace. This deadline is consistent across plan years and is not subject to change based on holidays or other calendar shifts, meaning it is observed regardless of whether the first Monday falls on June 1st or later in the month. By establishing a uniform cutoff, CMS enables effective planning and coordination in the administration of prescription drug benefits under Medicare. In summary, the FIRST MONDAY OF JUNE is a mandatory compliance date for PDP Sponsors to formally communicate their nonrenewal decisions to CMS, ensuring orderly transitions and regulatory adherence within the Medicare Part D program.|1

109|42 CFR § 423.265(B)(4)|42 CFR § 423.265(B)(4) is a regulation within the Code of Federal Regulations that governs the Medicare Part D prescription drug benefit program. This provision establishes that when a pharmacy or a plan sponsor fails to reach an agreement on a bid—specifically, a bid for reimbursement rates or contract terms—such a failure does not entitle the party to appeal the decision. Furthermore, the regulation explicitly states that failure to agree on a bid results in the automatic non-renewal of the contract. This means that if a pharmacy or plan sponsor does not successfully negotiate and finalize a bid agreement with the Medicare contractor or plan, their existing contract will not be extended, and they will lose their participation in the program unless they reapply and are selected under a new process. The regulation underscores that this outcome is not subject to administrative appeal, thereby limiting the avenues for dispute resolution in the event of bid disagreement. This provision is designed to ensure timely and efficient contract management within the Medicare Part D framework, promoting stability and continuity in drug coverage for beneficiaries. By removing the possibility of appeal and tying contract renewal directly to successful bid agreement, the regulation reinforces the importance of timely negotiation and compliance with bid requirements. It applies to both pharmacy providers and plan sponsors participating in the Medicare Part D program, ensuring a uniform standard across the system. The regulation reflects a policy intent to maintain program integrity and operational efficiency by preventing indefinite contract extensions based on unresolved bid disputes. In summary, 42 CFR § 423.265(B)(4) clarifies that failure to agree on a bid is a final determination that both terminates the possibility of contract renewal and precludes the right to appeal, thereby streamlining the administrative process and reinforcing accountability in the Medicare Part D contracting system.|1

The purpose of this notice is to ensure that beneficiaries have sufficient time to review their coverage options and make informed decisions about their prescription drug plan for the upcoming year. The requirement applies uniformly to all PDP Sponsors, regardless of plan type or size, and is designed to promote continuity of care and reduce the risk of coverage gaps during the transition period between plans. The notice must be delivered in a clear, accessible format and must include key information such as the effective date of nonrenewal, the reasons for nonrenewal (if applicable), and guidance on how enrollees can enroll in a new plan during the annual enrollment period. This 90-day window serves as a critical safeguard for Medicare beneficiaries, particularly those with chronic conditions or complex medication needs, who may be adversely affected by abrupt changes in their drug coverage. By enforcing a standardized timeframe for communication, the rule enhances transparency and accountability in the Medicare Part D program. The requirement is consistent with broader regulatory efforts to protect beneficiaries and ensure a stable, predictable enrollment process. While the specific language of the notice may vary slightly depending on the sponsor, the core obligation remains the same: to provide timely, accurate, and actionable information to enrollees at least 90 days prior to contract nonrenewal. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide applicable beneficiaries manufacturer discounts on applicable drugs both in the initial and catastrophic coverage phases of the Part D benefit in accordance with the requirements of § 1860D-14C of the Act and all applicable guidance, including the Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance.
5. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide all Part D enrollees with the option to participate in the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan in accordance with the requirements of § 1860D2(b)(2)(E) of the Act and all applicable guidance, including the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan: Final Part One Guidance on Select Topics, Implementation of Section

## Article II

## Functions to be Performed by PDP Sponsor

1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments and Medicare Prescription Payment Plan: Final Part Two Guidance on Select Topics, Implementation of Section 1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments.

## C. DISSEMINATION OF PLAN INFORMATION

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the information required in 42 CFR § 423.48.
2. PDP Sponsor acknowledges that CMS releases to the public the following data, consistent with 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart K:
3. (a) Summary reconciled Part D payment data after the reconciliation of Part D payments, as provided in 42 CFR § 423.505(o)(1); and
4. (b) Part D Medical Loss Ratio data for the contract year, as described at 42 CFR § 423.2490.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to disclose information to beneficiaries in the manner and the form specified by CMS under 42 CFR § 423.128 and 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart V.

## D. QUALITY ASSURANCE/UTILIZATION MANAGEMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate quality assurance, drug utilization management, drug management, and medication therapy management programs, and to support electronic prescribing, in accordance with Subpart D of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to address and resolve complaints received by CMS against the PDP Sponsor through the CMS complaint tracking system as required in 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(22).
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain a Part D summary plan rating score of at least 3 stars as required by 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(26).
4. PDP Sponsor agrees to pass an essential operations test prior to the start of the benefit year. This provision only applies to new sponsors that have not previously entered into a Part D contract with CMS and neither it, nor another subsidiary of the applicant's parent organization, is offering Part D benefits during the current year. [42 CFR § 423.505(b)(27)]

## E. APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all requirements in Subpart M of 42 CFR Part 423 governing coverage determinations, grievances and appeals, and formulary exceptions, and the applicable provisions of Subpart U.

## F. PAYMENT TO PDP SPONSOR

1. PDP Sponsor and CMS agree that payment under this contract is governed by the rules in Subpart G of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all applicable Federal laws and regulations, guidance, and authorities pertaining to claims and debt collections. In the event that the Government determines that PDP Sponsor has been overpaid, PDP Sponsor agrees to return those overpaid monies back to the Government.

## G. BID SUBMISSION AND REVIEW

If PDP Sponsor intends to participate in the Part D program for the next program year, PDP Sponsor agrees to submit the next year's bid, including all required information on premiums, benefits, and cost-sharing, by the applicable due date, as provided in Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 so that CMS and the PDP Sponsor may conduct negotiations regarding the terms and conditions of the proposed bid and benefit plan renewal.

## H. STATE LAW AND LICENSURE REQUIREMENTS

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with State law to the extent that it is not preempted by Federal law as described in Subpart I of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees that where it is operating in a State using a waiver granted pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.410, such waiver shall be valid for three consecutive program years. PDP Sponsor agrees that expiration of the licensure waiver (and the failure to obtain a license from the relevant State) may be the basis for CMS deleting from PDP Sponsor's service area those PDP Regions affected by the waiver expiration. CMS may terminate or non-renew PDP Sponsor's contract where the expiration of the waiver results in PDP Sponsor not being qualified to offer a PDP plan in any PDP Region.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees that where it is operating in a State using a waiver granted pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.415, such waiver shall be valid for the period that the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services determines is appropriate for timely processing of PDP Sponsor's license application by
2| affected by the waiver expiration. CMS may terminate or non-renew PDP Sponsor's contract where the expiration of the waiver results in PDP Sponsor not being qualified to offer a PDP plan in any PDP Region.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees that where it is operating in a State using a waiver granted pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.415, such waiver shall be valid for the period that the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services determines is appropriate for timely processing of PDP Sponsor's license application by the State, but in no case for more than one year only, beginning on January 1 of the contract year for which CMS granted the waiver.

## I. COORDINATION WITH OTHER PRESCRIPTION DRUG COVERAGE

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the coordination requirements with State Pharmacy Assistance Programs (SPAPs) and plans that provide other prescription drug coverage as described in Subpart J of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with Medicare Secondary Payer procedures as described in 42 CFR § 423.462.

## J. SERVICE AREA AND PHARMACY ACCESS

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits in the service area for which it has been approved by CMS utilizing a pharmacy network and formulary approved by CMS that meet the requirements of 42 CFR § 423.120.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits through out-of-network pharmacies according to 42 CFR § 423.124.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide benefits by means of point of service systems to adjudicate prescription drug claims in a timely and efficient manner in compliance with CMS standards, except when necessary to provide access in underserved areas, I/T/U pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100), and long-term care pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100) according to 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(17).
4. PDP Sponsor agrees to contract with any pharmacy that meets PDP Sponsor's reasonable and relevant standard terms and conditions according to 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(18), including making standard contracts available on request in accordance with the timelines specified in the regulation.

## K. EFFECTIVE COMPLIANCE PROGRAM/PROGRAM INTEGRITY

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to adopt and implement an effective compliance program that applies to its Part D-related operations, consistent with 42 CFR § 423.504(b)(4)(vi).
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide notice based on best knowledge, information, and belief to CMS of any integrity items related to payments from governmental entities, both Federal and State, for healthcare or prescription drug services that would have been reported as part of Table A. of the Business Integrity section of the PDP application. These items include any investigations, legal actions or matters subject to arbitration brought involving the PDP Sponsor (or the PDP Sponsor's firm if applicable) and its subcontractors (excluding contracted network providers), including any key management or executive staff, or any major shareholders (5% or more), by a government agency (State or Federal) on matters relating to payments from governmental entities, both Federal and State, for healthcare and/or prescription drug services. In providing the notice, the PDP Sponsor shall keep the Government informed of when the integrity item is initiated and when it is closed. Notice should be provided of the details concerning any resolution and monetary payments as well as any settlement agreements or corporate integrity agreements.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide notice based on best knowledge, information, and belief to CMS in the event PDP Sponsor or any of its subcontractors is criminally convicted or has a civil judgment entered against it for fraudulent activities or is sanctioned under any Federal program involving the provision of health care or prescription drug services.

## L. LOW-INCOME SUBSIDY

PDP Sponsor agrees that it will participate in the administration of subsidies for low-income subsidy eligible individuals according to Subpart P of 42 CFR Part 423.

## M. COMMUNICATION WITH CMS

PDP Sponsor agrees that it shall maintain the capacity to communicate with CMS electronically in accordance with CMS requirements.

## N. BENEFICIARY FINANCIAL PROTECTIONS

PDP Sponsor agrees to afford its enrollees protection from liability for payment of fees that are the obligation of PDP Sponsor in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(g).

## O. RELATIONSHIP WITH FIRST TIER, DOWNSTREAM, AND RELATED ENTITIES

1. PDP Sponsor agrees that it maintains ultimate responsibility for adhering to and otherwise fully complying with all terms and conditions of this contract with CMS. [42 CFR § 423.505(i)]
2. PDP Sponsor shall ensure that any contracts or agreements with first tier, downstream, and related entities performing functions on PDP Sponsor's behalf related to the operation of the Part D benefit are in compliance with 42 CFR § 423.505(i).
3. PDP Sponsor agrees not to employ or contract with an individual or entity who is excluded from participation in Medicare under Section 1128 or 1128A of the Social Security Act (or with an entity that employs or contracts with an excluded individual or entity) for provision of any of the services listed in 42 CFR § 423.752(a)(6).

## P. CERTIFICATION OF DATA THAT DETERMINE PAYMENT

PDP Sponsor must provide certifications in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(k).

## Q. ENROLLMENT RELATED COSTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to payment of fees established by CMS for cost sharing of enrollment related costs in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.6.

## R. PDP SPONSOR REIMBURSEMENT TO PHARMACIES [42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(21) and 423.520]

1. If a PDP Sponsor uses a standard for reimbursement of pharmacies based on the cost of a drug, PDP Sponsor will update such standard not less frequently than once every 7
4|rollees, through this notice or outbound

- telephone calls, information on alternatives available for obtaining qualified prescription drug coverage within the PDP region, including Medicare AdvantagePrescription Drug plans, Medicare cost plans offering a Part D plan, and other PDPs, and must receive CMS approval of notices or scripts prior to their use.
- C. If PDP Sponsor does not renew a contract, CMS cannot enter into a contract with PDP Sponsor or with an organization whose covered persons, as defined in 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(4), also served as covered persons for the nonrenewing PDP Sponsor for 2 years in the PDP region or regions served by the contract unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. If a PDP Sponsor does not renew any of its plan benefit packages (PBPs) in a PDP region, CMS does not approve plan bids submitted by the organization in that PDP region for 2 years unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. - D. If PDP Sponsor does not renew a contract, it must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(5).

## Article VIII Modification or Termination of Contract

## A. CONTRACT MODIFICATION OR TERMINATION BY MUTUAL CONSENT

1. This contract may be modified or terminated at any time by written mutual consent of the parties. If the PDP Sponsor submits a request to end the term of this contract after the deadline provided in 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(2)(i), CMS may mutually consent to the contract termination if the contract termination does not negatively affect the administration of the Medicare Part D Program.
2. If this contract is terminated by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must provide notice to its Medicare enrollees and the general public in accordance with CMS's instructions.
3. As set forth in 42 CFR § 423.508, if the contract is modified by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must notify its Medicare enrollees of any changes that CMS determines are appropriate for notification according to the process and timeframes specified by CMS.
4. If a contract is terminated under this section, PDP Sponsor must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files.
5. If a contract is terminated under this section, CMS cannot enter into a new contract or service area expansion in the PDP region or regions served by the contract with PDP Sponsor or with an organization whose covered persons, as defined in 42 CFR § 423.508(f), also served as covered persons for the terminating PDP Sponsor for a period of up to 2 years unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. A PDP Sponsor that agrees to terminate its offering of PBPs in a PDP region also agrees that it will not be eligible to apply to resume offering plans in that region for 2 years. [42 CFR § 423.508(e)]

## B. TERMINATION OF CONTRACT BY CMS

CMS may terminate the contract in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.509.

## C. TERMINATION OF CONTRACT BY PDP SPONSOR

PDP Sponsor may terminate the contract only in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.510.

## Article IX Compliance and Enforcement Actions

## A. INTERMEDIATE SANCTIONS

Consistent with Subpart O of 42 CFR Part 423, PDP Sponsor shall be subject to sanctions and civil money penalties.

## B. COMPLIANCE ACTIONS AND PAST PERFORMANCE

CMS may determine that the PDP Sponsor is out of compliance with a Part D requirement and take compliance actions as described in 42 CFR § 423.505(n) or issue intermediate sanctions as defined in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart O. [42 CFR § 423.505(n)]

## Article X Severability

Severability of the contract shall be in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.504(e).

## Article XI Miscellaneous

## A. DEFINITIONS

Terms not otherwise defined in this contract shall have the meaning given to such terms in §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act and 42 CFR Part 423.

## B. ALTERATION TO ORIGINAL CONTRACT TERMS

PDP Sponsor agrees and attests that it has not altered in any way the terms of the PDP contract presented for signature by CMS. PDP Sponsor agrees that any alterations to the original text that PDP Sponsor may make to this contract shall not be binding on the parties.

## C. ADDITIONAL CONTRACT TERMS

PDP Sponsor agrees to include in this contract other terms and conditions in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(j).

- D. Pursuant to § 13112 of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA), PDP Sponsor agrees that as it implements, acquires, or upgrades its health information technology systems, it shall utilize, where available, health information technology systems and products that meet standards and implementation specifications adopted under § 3004 of the Public Health Service Act, as amended by § 13101 of the ARRA.

- F. Business Continuity: PDP Sponsor agrees to develop, maintain, and implement a business continuity plan as required by 42 CFR § 423.505(p).
- G. The PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with applicable anti-discrimination laws, including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (and pertinent regulations at 45 CFR Part 80), § 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (and pertinent regulations at 45 CFR Part 84), and the Age Discrimination Act of 1975 (and pertinent regulations at

- G. The PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with applicable anti-discrimination laws, including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (and pertinent regulations at 45 CFR Part 80), § 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (and pertinent regulations at 45 CFR Part 84), and the Age Discrimination Act of 1975 (and pertinent regulations at 45 CFR Part 91). This regulation establishes the framework under which PDP Sponsors—organizations responsible for administering Medicare Part D prescription drug plans—enter into and maintain contracts with CMS. Furthermore, the regulation explicitly states that failure to agree on a bid results in the automatic non-renewal of the contract. This means that if a pharmacy or plan sponsor does not successfully negotiate and finalize a bid agreement with the Medicare contractor or plan, their existing contract will not be extended, and they will lose their participation in the program unless they reapply and are selected under a new process. The regulation underscores that this outcome is not subject to administrative appeal, thereby limiting the avenues for dispute resolution in the event of bid disagreement. This provision is designed to ensure timely and efficient contract management within the Medicare Part D framework, promoting stability and continuity in drug coverage for beneficiaries. By removing the possibility of appeal and tying contract renewal directly to successful bid agreement, the regulation reinforces the importance of timely negotiation and compliance with bid requirements. It applies to both pharmacy providers and plan sponsors participating in the Medicare Part D program, ensuring a uniform standard across the system. The regulation reflects a policy intent to maintain program integrity and operational efficiency by preventing indefinite contract extensions based on unresolved bid disputes. In summary, 42 CFR § 423.265(B)(4) clarifies that failure to agree on a bid is a final determination that both terminates the possibility of contract renewal and precludes the right to appeal, thereby streamlining the administrative process and reinforcing accountability in the Medicare Part D contracting system.|1

## Article I

## Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan

## D. QUALITY ASSURANCE/UTILIZATION MANAGEMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate quality assurance, drug utilization management, drug management, and medication therapy management programs, and to support electronic prescribing, in accordance with Subpart D of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to address and resolve complaints received by CMS against the PDP Sponsor through the CMS complaint tracking system as required in 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(22).

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all requirements in Subpart M of 42 CFR Part 423 governing coverage determinations, grievances and appeals, and formulary exceptions, and the applicable provisions of Subpart U.

1. PDP Sponsor and CMS agree that payment under this contract is governed by the rules in Subpart G of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all applicable Federal laws and regulations, guidance, and authorities pertaining to claims and debt collections. In the event that the Government determines that PDP Sponsor has been overpaid, PDP Sponsor agrees to return those overpaid monies back to the Government.

3. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide benefits by means of point of service systems to adjudicate prescription drug claims in a timely and efficient manner in compliance with CMS standards, except when necessary to provide access in underserved areas, I/T/U pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100), and long-term care pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100) according to 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(17).

PDP Sponsor agrees to provide notice based on best knowledge, information, and belief to CMS of any integrity items related to payments from governmental entities, both Federal and State, for healthcare or prescription drug services that would have been reported as part of Table A. of the Business Integrity section of the PDP application. PDP Sponsor agrees that it will participate in the administration of subsidies for low-income subsidy eligible individuals according to Subpart P of 42 CFR Part 423.

PDP Sponsor agrees that it shall maintain the capacity to communicate with CMS electronically in accordance with CMS requirements.

## N. BENEFICIARY FINANCIAL PROTECTIONS

PDP Sponsor agrees to afford its enrollees protection from liability for payment of fees that are the obligation of PDP Sponsor in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(g).

1. PDP Sponsor agrees that it maintains ultimate responsibility for adhering to and otherwise fully complying with all terms and conditions of this contract with CMS. [42 CFR § 423.505(i)]

PDP Sponsor must provide certifications in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(k).

1. In accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507, PDP Sponsor will be determined qualified to renew its contract annually only if PDP Sponsor has not provided CMS with a notice of intention not to renew in accordance with Article VII of this contract.

This means that if a pharmacy or plan sponsor does not successfully negotiate and finalize a bid agreement with the Medicare contractor or plan, their existing contract will not be extended, and they will lose their participation in the program unless they reapply and are selected under a new process. The regulation underscores that this outcome is not subject to administrative appeal, thereby limiting the avenues for dispute resolution in the event of bid disagreement. This provision is designed to ensure timely and efficient contract management within the Medicare Part D framework, promoting stability and continuity in drug coverage for beneficiaries. By removing the possibility of appeal and tying contract renewal directly to successful bid agreement, the regulation reinforces the importance of timely negotiation and compliance with bid requirements. It applies to both pharmacy providers and plan sponsors participating in the Medicare Part D program, ensuring a uniform standard across the system. The regulation reflects a policy intent to maintain program integrity and operational efficiency by preventing indefinite contract extensions based on unresolved bid disputes. ## Functions to be Performed by PDP Sponsor

1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments and Medicare Prescription Payment Plan: Final Part Two Guidance on Select Topics, Implementation of Section 1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments.

## C. DISSEMINATION OF PLAN INFORMATION

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the information required in 42 CFR § 423.48.

3. (a) Summary reconciled Part D payment data after the reconciliation of Part D payments, as provided in 42 CFR § 423.505(o)(1); and
4. (b) Part D Medical Loss Ratio data for the contract year, as described at 42 CFR § 423.2490.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to disclose information to beneficiaries in the manner and the form specified by CMS under 42 CFR § 423.128 and 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart V.

## D. QUALITY ASSURANCE/UTILIZATION MANAGEMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate quality assurance, drug utilization management, drug management, and medication therapy management programs, and to support electronic prescribing, in accordance with Subpart D of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to address and resolve complaints received by CMS against the PDP Sponsor through the CMS complaint tracking system as required in 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(22).
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain a Part D summary plan rating score of at least 3 stars as required by 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(26).

This provision only applies to new sponsors that have not previously entered into a Part D contract with CMS and neither it, nor another subsidiary of the applicant's parent organization, is offering Part D benefits during the current year. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all requirements in Subpart M of 42 CFR Part 423 governing coverage determinations, grievances and appeals, and formulary exceptions, and the applicable provisions of Subpart U.

1. PDP Sponsor and CMS agree that payment under this contract is governed by the rules in Subpart G of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all applicable Federal laws and regulations, guidance, and authorities pertaining to claims and debt collections. If PDP Sponsor intends to participate in the Part D program for the next program year, PDP Sponsor agrees to submit the next year's bid, including all required information on premiums, benefits, and cost-sharing, by the applicable due date, as provided in Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 so that CMS and the PDP Sponsor may conduct negotiations regarding the terms and conditions of the proposed bid and benefit plan renewal.

Article V

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with (a) applicable Federal laws and regulations designed to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse, including, but not limited to, applicable provisions of Federal criminal law, the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 3729 et seq.), and the anti-kickback provision of § 1128B of the Act; (b) applicable Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) rules at 45 CFR Parts 160, 162, and 164; and (c) all other applicable Federal statutes and regulations.

## Article VI Contract Term and Renewal

## A. TERM OF CONTRACT

This contract is effective from the date of CMS's authorized representative's signature through December 31, 2025. This contract shall be renewable for successive one-year periods thereafter according to 42 CFR § 423.506.

## B. QUALIFICATION TO RENEW A CONTRACT

1. In accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507, PDP Sponsor will be determined qualified to renew its contract annually only if PDP Sponsor has not provided CMS with a notice of intention not to renew in accordance with Article VII of this contract.

3. (a) CMS in writing by the first Monday of June in the year in which the current contract period ends;

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the coordination requirements with State Pharmacy Assistance Programs (SPAPs) and plans that provide other prescription drug coverage as described in Subpart J of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with Medicare Secondary Payer procedures as described in 42 CFR § 423.462.

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits in the service area for which it has been approved by CMS utilizing a pharmacy network and formulary approved by CMS that meet the requirements of 42 CFR § 423.120.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits through out-of-network pharmacies according to 42 CFR § 423.124.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide benefits by means of point of service systems to adjudicate prescription drug claims in a timely and efficient manner in compliance with CMS standards, except when necessary to provide access in underserved areas, I/T/U pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100), and long-term care pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100) according to 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(17).

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to adopt and implement an effective compliance program that applies to its Part D-related operations, consistent with 42 CFR § 423.504(b)(4)(vi).
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide notice based on best knowledge, information, and belief to CMS of any integrity items related to payments from governmental entities, both Federal and State, for healthcare or prescription drug services that would have been reported as part of Table A. of the Business Integrity section of the PDP application. 89|BENEFICIARY|MEDICARE PRESCRIPTION PAYMENT PLAN|The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan (MPPP) is a financial assistance program designed to help beneficiaries manage the cost of prescription drugs. Beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare can choose to participate in this plan to pay for their prescription medications in manageable installments rather than facing large out-of-pocket expenses at the time of purchase. The program is specifically intended to reduce the financial burden associated with prescription drug costs, particularly for individuals with high medication needs or limited financial resources. By enrolling in the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan, beneficiaries can spread their drug payments over time, making it easier to budget and maintain consistent access to necessary medications. Participation in the plan is voluntary, and beneficiaries may enroll at any time during the year, subject to program guidelines and availability. The installment payments are typically deducted from the beneficiary’s monthly Medicare Part B premium, streamlining the payment process and ensuring that costs are addressed consistently. This arrangement helps prevent financial strain while promoting medication adherence, which is critical for managing chronic conditions and maintaining overall health. CMS also holds the authority to grant waivers when necessary and ensures that PDP Sponsors adhere to federal standards and program requirements. Through ongoing compliance monitoring and enforcement actions, CMS maintains program integrity and protects beneficiaries' access to affordable prescription drugs. Additionally, CMS is responsible for data dissemination related to the Part D program, ensuring transparency and supporting informed decision-making by stakeholders. As the primary federal entity governing Medicare Part D, CMS ensures the program operates efficiently, effectively, and in alignment with legislative mandates. Its comprehensive oversight spans from initial plan sponsor applications and bid evaluations to ongoing contract management and performance evaluation. The agency’s responsibilities are essential to the stability and success of the Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Benefit, which provides prescription drug coverage to millions of Medicare beneficiaries across the United States.|20

## I. COORDINATION WITH OTHER PRESCRIPTION DRUG COVERAGE

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the coordination requirements with State Pharmacy Assistance Programs (SPAPs) and plans that provide other prescription drug coverage as described in Subpart J of 42 CFR Part 423.

## J. SERVICE AREA AND PHARMACY ACCESS

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits in the service area for which it has been approved by CMS utilizing a pharmacy network and formulary approved by CMS that meet the requirements of 42 CFR § 423.120.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits through out-of-network pharmacies according to 42 CFR § 423.124.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide benefits by means of point of service systems to adjudicate prescription drug claims in a timely and efficient manner in compliance with CMS standards, except when necessary to provide access in underserved areas, I/T/U pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100), and long-term care pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100) according to 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(17).

2. PDP Sponsor agrees that it will participate in the administration of subsidies for low-income subsidy eligible individuals according to Subpart P of 42 CFR Part 423.

PDP Sponsor agrees that it shall maintain the capacity to communicate with CMS electronically in accordance with CMS requirements.

PDP Sponsor agrees to afford its enrollees protection from liability for payment of fees that are the obligation of PDP Sponsor in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(g).

3. As set forth in 42 CFR § 423.508, if the contract is modified by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must notify its Medicare enrollees of any changes that CMS determines are appropriate for notification according to the process and timeframes specified by CMS.
4. If a contract is terminated under this section, PDP Sponsor must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files.
5. CMS may terminate the contract in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.509.

## C. TERMINATION OF CONTRACT BY PDP SPONSOR

PDP Sponsor may terminate the contract only in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.510.

## Article IX Compliance and Enforcement Actions

## A. INTERMEDIATE SANCTIONS

Consistent with Subpart O of 42 CFR Part 423, PDP Sponsor shall be subject to sanctions and civil money penalties.

## B. COMPLIANCE ACTIONS AND PAST PERFORMANCE

CMS may determine that the PDP Sponsor is out of compliance with a Part D requirement and take compliance actions as described in 42 CFR § 423.505(n) or issue intermediate sanctions as defined in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart O. [42 CFR § 423.505(n)]

## Article X Severability

Severability of the contract shall be in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.504(e).

## Article XI Miscellaneous

## A. DEFINITIONS

Terms not otherwise defined in this contract shall have the meaning given to such terms in §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act and 42 CFR Part 423.

## B. ALTERATION TO ORIGINAL CONTRACT TERMS

PDP Sponsor agrees and attests that it has not altered in any way the terms of the PDP contract presented for signature by CMS. PDP Sponsor agrees that any alterations to the original text that PDP Sponsor may make to this contract shall not be binding on the parties.

PDP Sponsor agrees to include in this contract other terms and conditions in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(j).

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the coordination requirements with State Pharmacy Assistance Programs (SPAPs) and plans that provide other prescription drug coverage as described in Subpart J of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with Medicare Secondary Payer procedures as described in 42 CFR § 423.462.

## J. SERVICE AREA AND PHARMACY ACCESS

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits in the service area for which it has been approved by CMS utilizing a pharmacy network and formulary approved by CMS that meet the requirements of 42 CFR § 423.120.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide Part D benefits through out-of-network pharmacies according to 42 CFR § 423.124.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide benefits by means of point of service systems to adjudicate prescription drug claims in a timely and efficient manner in compliance with CMS standards, except when necessary to provide access in underserved areas, I/T/U pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100), and long-term care pharmacies (as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100) according to 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(17).

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to adopt and implement an effective compliance program that applies to its Part D-related operations, consistent with 42 CFR § 423.504(b)(4)(vi).
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide notice based on best knowledge, information, and belief to CMS of any integrity items related to payments from governmental entities, both Federal and State, for healthcare or prescription drug services that would have been reported as part of Table A. of the Business Integrity section of the PDP application. These items include any investigations, legal actions or matters subject to arbitration brought involving the PDP Sponsor (or the PDP Sponsor's firm if applicable) and its subcontractors (excluding contracted network providers), including any key management or executive staff, or any major shareholders (5% or more), by a government agency (State or Federal) on matters relating to payments from governmental entities, both Federal and State, for healthcare and/or prescription drug services. In providing the notice, the PDP Sponsor shall keep the Government informed of when the integrity item is initiated and when it is closed. Notice should be provided of the details concerning any resolution and monetary payments as well as any settlement agreements or corporate integrity agreements.
3. ## L. LOW-INCOME SUBSIDY

PDP Sponsor agrees that it will participate in the administration of subsidies for low-income subsidy eligible individuals according to Subpart P of 42 CFR Part 423.

## M. COMMUNICATION WITH CMS

PDP Sponsor agrees that it shall maintain the capacity to communicate with CMS electronically in accordance with CMS requirements.

## N. BENEFICIARY FINANCIAL PROTECTIONS

PDP Sponsor agrees to afford its enrollees protection from liability for payment of fees that are the obligation of PDP Sponsor in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(g).

## O. RELATIONSHIP WITH FIRST TIER, DOWNSTREAM, AND RELATED ENTITIES

1. PDP Sponsor agrees that it maintains ultimate responsibility for adhering to and otherwise fully complying with all terms and conditions of this contract with CMS. [42 CFR § 423.505(i)]
2. PDP Sponsor shall ensure that any contracts or agreements with first tier, downstream, and related entities performing functions on PDP Sponsor's behalf related to the operation of the Part D benefit are in compliance with 42 CFR § 423.505(i).
3. ## P. CERTIFICATION OF DATA THAT DETERMINE PAYMENT

PDP Sponsor must provide certifications in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(k).

Between

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (hereinafter referred to as 'CMS')

## <<CONTRACT\_NAME>>

(a Prescription Drug Plan Sponsor, hereinafter referred to as 'PDP Sponsor')

## Article I

## Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate one or more Medicare Voluntary Prescription Drug Plans (hereinafter referred to as a 'PDP'), as described in its application and related materials submitted to CMS for Medicare approval, including but not limited to all the attestations contained therein, and in compliance with the provisions of this contract, which incorporates in its entirety the 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, released on January 9, 2024 (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'the contract'). PDP Sponsor also agrees to operate in accordance with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Act, the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings. Except as provided in paragraph (C) of this Article, this contract is deemed to incorporate any changes that are required by statute to be implemented during the term of this contract and any regulations implementing or interpreting such statutory provisions.
- B. CMS agrees to perform its obligations to PDP Sponsor consistent with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31), the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings.
- C. CMS agrees that it will not implement, other than at the beginning of a calendar year, regulations under 42 CFR Part 423 that impose new, significant regulatory requirements on PDP Sponsor. This provision does not apply to new requirements mandated by statute. [42 CFR § 423.516]
- D. If PDP Sponsor had a contract with CMS for Contract Year 2024 under the contract ID number designated above, this document is considered a renewal of the existing contract. While the terms of this document supersede the terms of the 2024 contract, the parties' execution of this contract does not extinguish or interrupt any pending obligations or actions that may have arisen under the 2024 or prior year contracts.
- E. This contract is in no way intended to supersede or modify 42 CFR Part 423. Failure to reference a regulatory requirement in this contract does not affect the applicability of such requirements to PDP Sponsor and CMS.

## A. ENROLLMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to accept new enrollments, make enrollments effective, process voluntary disenrollments, and limit involuntary disenrollments, as described in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart B.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the prohibition in 42 CFR § 423.104(b) on discrimination in beneficiary enrollment.
3. PDP Sponsor shall accept enrollment applications from individuals who change their election during the open enrollment period for individuals enrolled in Medicare Advantage described in 42 CFR § 422.62(a)(3), as required by 42 CFR § 423.38(e).

## B. PRESCRIPTION DRUG BENEFIT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the basic prescription drug coverage as defined under 42 CFR § 423.100 and, to the extent applicable, supplemental benefits as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100 and in accordance with Subpart C of 42 CFR Part 423. PDP Sponsor also agrees to provide Part D benefits as described in PDP Sponsor's bid(s) approved each year by CMS (as referenced in the Medicare Advantage Attestation of Benefit Plan, which is included in the contracting materials, and to be replaced each year upon renewal of the contract to reflect PDP Sponsor's approved bids for the succeeding contract year).

If PDP Sponsor does not renew a contract, CMS cannot enter into a contract with PDP Sponsor or with an organization whose covered persons, as defined in 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(4), also served as covered persons for the nonrenewing PDP Sponsor for 2 years in the PDP region or regions served by the contract unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. If a PDP Sponsor does not renew any of its plan benefit packages (PBPs) in a PDP region, CMS does not approve plan bids submitted by the organization in that PDP region for 2 years unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. - D. If PDP Sponsor does not renew a contract, it must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(5).

## Article VIII Modification or Termination of Contract

## A. CONTRACT MODIFICATION OR TERMINATION BY MUTUAL CONSENT

1. This contract may be modified or terminated at any time by written mutual consent of the parties. If the PDP Sponsor submits a request to end the term of this contract after the deadline provided in 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(2)(i), CMS may mutually consent to the contract termination if the contract termination does not negatively affect the administration of the Medicare Part D Program.
2. If this contract is terminated by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must provide notice to its Medicare enrollees and the general public in accordance with CMS's instructions.
3. As set forth in 42 CFR § 423.508, if the contract is modified by mutual consent, PDP Sponsor must notify its Medicare enrollees of any changes that CMS determines are appropriate for notification according to the process and timeframes specified by CMS.
4. If a contract is terminated under this section, PDP Sponsor must ensure the timely transfer of any data or files.
5. If a contract is terminated under this section, CMS cannot enter into a new contract or service area expansion in the PDP region or regions served by the contract with PDP Sponsor or with an organization whose covered persons, as defined in 42 CFR § 423.508(f), also served as covered persons for the terminating PDP Sponsor for a period of up to 2 years unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. CMS may terminate the contract in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.509.

## C. TERMINATION OF CONTRACT BY PDP SPONSOR

PDP Sponsor may terminate the contract only in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.510.

## Article IX Compliance and Enforcement Actions

## A. INTERMEDIATE SANCTIONS

Consistent with Subpart O of 42 CFR Part 423, PDP Sponsor shall be subject to sanctions and civil money penalties.

## B. COMPLIANCE ACTIONS AND PAST PERFORMANCE

CMS may determine that the PDP Sponsor is out of compliance with a Part D requirement and take compliance actions as described in 42 CFR § 423.505(n) or issue intermediate sanctions as defined in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart O. [42 CFR § 423.505(n)]

## Article X Severability

Severability of the contract shall be in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.504(e).

## Article XI Miscellaneous

## A. DEFINITIONS

Terms not otherwise defined in this contract shall have the meaning given to such terms in §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act and 42 CFR Part 423.

## B. ALTERATION TO ORIGINAL CONTRACT TERMS

PDP Sponsor agrees and attests that it has not altered in any way the terms of the PDP contract presented for signature by CMS. PDP Sponsor agrees that any alterations to the original text that PDP Sponsor may make to this contract shall not be binding on the parties.

## C. ADDITIONAL CONTRACT TERMS

PDP Sponsor agrees to include in this contract other terms and conditions in accordance with 42 CFR § 423.505(j).

- D. Pursuant to § 13112 of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA), PDP Sponsor agrees that as it implements, acquires, or upgrades its health information technology systems, it shall utilize, where available, health information technology systems and products that meet standards and implementation specifications adopted under § 3004 of the Public Health Service Act, as amended by § 13101 of the ARRA.
- E. PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain a fiscally sound operation by at least maintaining a positive net worth (total assets exceed total liabilities) as required in 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(23).

The PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with applicable anti-discrimination laws, including Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (and pertinent regulations at 45 CFR Part 80), § 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (and pertinent regulations at 45 CFR Part 84), and the Age Discrimination Act of 1975 (and pertinent regulations at

1. If a PDP Sponsor uses a standard for reimbursement of pharmacies based on the cost of a drug, PDP Sponsor will update such standard not less frequently than once every 7 days, beginning with an initial update on January 1 of each year, to accurately reflect the market price of the drug.

4. PDP Sponsor must ensure that a pharmacy located in, or having a contract with, a longterm care facility will have not less than 30 days (but not more than 90 days) to submit claims to PDP Sponsor for reimbursement.

PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain records and provide access in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.505(b)(10) and 423.505(i)(2).

## B. GENERAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

PDP Sponsor agrees to submit information to CMS according to 42 CFR §§ 423.505(f) and 423.514, and applicable Final Medicare Part D Reporting Guidance.

134|42 CFR § 423.504(E)|42 CFR § 423.504(E) is a provision within Title 42 of the Code of Federal Regulations, specifically under Part 423, which governs the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit. This section addresses the principle of severability in contract terms, ensuring contractual integrity in the event that one or more provisions are found to be legally invalid or unenforceable. The primary purpose of 42 CFR § 423.504(E) is to prevent the entire contract from being invalidated due to the failure of a single provision. By establishing a severability clause, the regulation ensures that if a court or regulatory authority determines that a specific term within a contract—such as one related to drug pricing, beneficiary coverage, or plan performance—is unlawful, unenforceable, or contrary to public policy, the remainder of the contract remains valid and enforceable. This provision supports regulatory stability and continuity in the Medicare Part D program by allowing contracts to withstand legal challenges without collapsing entirely. The section reflects a broader administrative principle used in federal contracting and regulatory frameworks, emphasizing that the intent of the parties and the overall effectiveness of the agreement should be preserved even when individual components are found wanting. As such, 42 CFR § 423.504(E) plays a critical role in maintaining the operational resilience of contracts between the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and Medicare Part D plan sponsors. It provides a legal safeguard that enables the continuation of essential prescription drug coverage for beneficiaries, even in the face of judicial or regulatory scrutiny of specific contractual terms. The regulation underscores the importance of drafting contracts with built-in flexibility and legal robustness, ensuring that the broader objectives of the Medicare program are not undermined by isolated legal defects. In summary, 42 CFR § 423.504(E) is a foundational provision that governs the severability of contract terms within the Medicare Part D framework, ensuring that the invalidity of one provision does not jeopardize the validity or enforceability of the entire agreement.|1

The primary purpose of the BUSINESS ASSOCIATE AGREEMENT is to establish a formal framework through which PDP Sponsors can securely share beneficiary data with CMS’s designated contractor, enabling the tracking and verification of cost-sharing amounts such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance. This data is critical for compliance with Medicare Part D requirements, including the calculation of the "donut hole" coverage gap and the determination of subsidy payments. The agreement ensures that the contracted entity, acting as a business associate under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), maintains appropriate safeguards to protect the privacy and security of protected health information (PHI) while fulfilling its responsibilities. By formalizing the relationship between PDP Sponsors and the CMS-contracted entity, the BUSINESS ASSOCIATE AGREEMENT supports regulatory compliance, enhances data integrity, and promotes transparency in the administration of Medicare Part D benefits. The legal requirement underscores the importance of coordinated data management across the Medicare ecosystem, ensuring that beneficiaries receive accurate coverage and that federal oversight remains effective. Overall, the BUSINESS ASSOCIATE AGREEMENT serves as a foundational component of the Medicare Part D program, aligning PDP Sponsors with federal mandates to improve accountability and beneficiary protection in prescription drug cost tracking.|1

1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments and Medicare Prescription Payment Plan: Final Part Two Guidance on Select Topics, Implementation of Section 1860D-2 of the Social Security Act for 2025, and Response to Relevant Comments.

## C. DISSEMINATION OF PLAN INFORMATION

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the information required in 42 CFR § 423.48.
2. PDP Sponsor acknowledges that CMS releases to the public the following data, consistent with 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart K:
3. (a) Summary reconciled Part D payment data after the reconciliation of Part D payments, as provided in 42 CFR § 423.505(o)(1); and
4. (b) Part D Medical Loss Ratio data for the contract year, as described at 42 CFR § 423.2490.
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to disclose information to beneficiaries in the manner and the form specified by CMS under 42 CFR § 423.128 and 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart V.

## D. QUALITY ASSURANCE/UTILIZATION MANAGEMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate quality assurance, drug utilization management, drug management, and medication therapy management programs, and to support electronic prescribing, in accordance with Subpart D of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to address and resolve complaints received by CMS against the PDP Sponsor through the CMS complaint tracking system as required in 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(22).
3. PDP Sponsor agrees to maintain a Part D summary plan rating score of at least 3 stars as required by 42 CFR § 423.505(b)(26).
4. PDP Sponsor agrees to pass an essential operations test prior to the start of the benefit year. This provision only applies to new sponsors that have not previously entered into a Part D contract with CMS and neither it, nor another subsidiary of the applicant's parent organization, is offering Part D benefits during the current year. [42 CFR § 423.505(b)(27)]

## E. APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES

PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all requirements in Subpart M of 42 CFR Part 423 governing coverage determinations, grievances and appeals, and formulary exceptions, and the applicable provisions of Subpart U.

## F. PAYMENT TO PDP SPONSOR

1. PDP Sponsor and CMS agree that payment under this contract is governed by the rules in Subpart G of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with all applicable Federal laws and regulations, guidance, and authorities pertaining to claims and debt collections. In the event that the Government determines that PDP Sponsor has been overpaid, PDP Sponsor agrees to return those overpaid monies back to the Government.

## G. BID SUBMISSION AND REVIEW

If PDP Sponsor intends to participate in the Part D program for the next program year, PDP Sponsor agrees to submit the next year's bid, including all required information on premiums, benefits, and cost-sharing, by the applicable due date, as provided in Subpart F of 42 CFR Part 423 so that CMS and the PDP Sponsor may conduct negotiations regarding the terms and conditions of the proposed bid and benefit plan renewal.

## H. STATE LAW AND LICENSURE REQUIREMENTS

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with State law to the extent that it is not preempted by Federal law as described in Subpart I of 42 CFR Part 423.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees that where it is operating in a State using a waiver granted pursuant to 42 CFR § 423.410, such waiver shall be valid for three consecutive program years. ## Article I

## Voluntary Medicare Prescription Drug Plan

- A. PDP Sponsor agrees to operate one or more Medicare Voluntary Prescription Drug Plans (hereinafter referred to as a 'PDP'), as described in its application and related materials submitted to CMS for Medicare approval, including but not limited to all the attestations contained therein, and in compliance with the provisions of this contract, which incorporates in its entirety the 2025 Solicitation for Applications for Medicare Prescription Drug Plan Contracts, released on January 9, 2024 (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'the contract'). PDP Sponsor also agrees to operate in accordance with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31) of the Act, the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings. Except as provided in paragraph (C) of this Article, this contract is deemed to incorporate any changes that are required by statute to be implemented during the term of this contract and any regulations implementing or interpreting such statutory provisions.
- B. CMS agrees to perform its obligations to PDP Sponsor consistent with §§ 1860D-1 through 1860D-43 of the Act (with the exception of §§ 1860D-22(a) and 1860D-31), the regulations at 42 CFR Part 423 (with the exception of Subparts Q, R, and S), and the solicitation, as well as all other applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies outlined in guidance, such as the Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Manual, the Medicare Communications and Marketing Guidelines, Final CY 2025 Part D Redesign Program Instructions, Medicare Part D Manufacturer Discount Program Final Guidance, Medicare Prescription Payment Plan Final Guidance, CMS Participant Guides, Health Plan Management System memos, Rate Announcement, and trainings.
- C. CMS agrees that it will not implement, other than at the beginning of a calendar year, regulations under 42 CFR Part 423 that impose new, significant regulatory requirements on PDP Sponsor. This provision does not apply to new requirements mandated by statute. [42 CFR § 423.516]
- D. If PDP Sponsor had a contract with CMS for Contract Year 2024 under the contract ID number designated above, this document is considered a renewal of the existing contract. While the terms of this document supersede the terms of the 2024 contract, the parties' execution of this contract does not extinguish or interrupt any pending obligations or actions that may have arisen under the 2024 or prior year contracts.
- E. This contract is in no way intended to supersede or modify 42 CFR Part 423. Failure to reference a regulatory requirement in this contract does not affect the applicability of such requirements to PDP Sponsor and CMS.

## A. ENROLLMENT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to accept new enrollments, make enrollments effective, process voluntary disenrollments, and limit involuntary disenrollments, as described in 42 CFR Part 423 Subpart B.
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to comply with the prohibition in 42 CFR § 423.104(b) on discrimination in beneficiary enrollment.
3. PDP Sponsor shall accept enrollment applications from individuals who change their election during the open enrollment period for individuals enrolled in Medicare Advantage described in 42 CFR § 422.62(a)(3), as required by 42 CFR § 423.38(e).

## B. PRESCRIPTION DRUG BENEFIT

1. PDP Sponsor agrees to provide the basic prescription drug coverage as defined under 42 CFR § 423.100 and, to the extent applicable, supplemental benefits as defined in 42 CFR § 423.100 and in accordance with Subpart C of 42 CFR Part 423. PDP Sponsor also agrees to provide Part D benefits as described in PDP Sponsor's bid(s) approved each year by CMS (as referenced in the Medicare Advantage Attestation of Benefit Plan, which is included in the contracting materials, and to be replaced each year upon renewal of the contract to reflect PDP Sponsor's approved bids for the succeeding contract year).
2. PDP Sponsor agrees to calculate and collect beneficiary premiums in accordance with 42 CFR §§ 423.286 and 423.293. PDP Sponsor also agrees to make a reasonable effort to identify all amounts incorrectly collected and to pay any other amounts due in accordance with

- telephone calls, information on alternatives available for obtaining qualified prescription drug coverage within the PDP region, including Medicare AdvantagePrescription Drug plans, Medicare cost plans offering a Part D plan, and other PDPs, and must receive CMS approval of notices or scripts prior to their use.
- C. If PDP Sponsor does not renew a contract, CMS cannot enter into a contract with PDP Sponsor or with an organization whose covered persons, as defined in 42 CFR § 423.507(a)(4), also served as covered persons for the nonrenewing PDP Sponsor for 2 years in the PDP region or regions served by the contract unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS. If a PDP Sponsor does not renew any of its plan benefit packages (PBPs) in a PDP region, CMS does not approve plan bids submitted by the organization in that PDP region for 2 years unless there are circumstances that warrant special consideration, as determined by CMS.
